title: Best Construction Payroll Software in 2026 [Compared for Trade Contractors]
summary: Compare the 8 best construction payroll software platforms of 2026, including Trayd, Miter, Foundation, Sage, ADP and QuickBooks, by best use, pros and cons.
body_markdown:
Last updated: October 23, 2026


[Construction payroll](https://www.buildtrayd.com/products/payroll/construction-payroll) is harder than regular payroll. Wage rates change by project, trade and jurisdiction, union fringes change by CBA, and certified payroll reports are due weekly. Below are the 8 construction payroll platforms contractors evaluate most often, with what each is best for and where each falls short.


## The best construction payroll software at a glance


Software


Best for


Trayd


Union and prevailing wage trade contractors who want a full construction ERP: payroll, compliance, field tracking, job costing and accounting in one system

Mid-sized contractors who want deep construction accounting and WIP reporting


Payroll4Construction


Contractors who want to outsource construction payroll entirely


Sage (100 Contractor / 300 CRE / Intacct)


Larger or multi-entity contractors already invested in Sage

Very small, non-union contractors on private work


QuickBooks Payroll


Small non-union contractors who already keep their books in QuickBooks


## What construction payroll software needs to do


A payroll system built for construction should handle:


-


**Project-level payroll.** Wage rates, tax jurisdictions and compliance rules tied to each project, not set company-wide.


-


**Prevailing wage and certified payroll.** Automated WH-347 generation, Davis-Bacon wage rate management, and fringe tracking by project and classification.


-


**Union CBA support.** CBA wage rates, fringe fund contributions, dues deductions and multi-local logic.


-


**Multi-state tax compliance.** Withholding based on where the work is performed.


-


**Field-to-payroll data flow.** Jobsite time flowing into payroll without re-entry.


-


**Job costing.** Fully burdened labor cost posted to the right project and cost code.


## 1. Trayd


[Trayd](https://www.buildtrayd.com/) is a full construction ERP built for specialty and trade contractors. It brings[payroll](https://www.buildtrayd.com/products/payroll/construction-payroll) ,[HR and onboarding](https://www.buildtrayd.com/products/hr-people-management/construction-worker-onboarding) ,[scheduling and dispatch](https://www.buildtrayd.com/products/scheduling/construction-crew-scheduling) ,[field and labor tracking](https://www.buildtrayd.com/products/field/construction-worker-app) ,[job costing](https://www.buildtrayd.com/solution/job-costing/construction-job-costing) , accounting and[compliance](https://www.buildtrayd.com/solution/compliance/certified-payroll) together in one system.


**Best for:** Union and trade contractors on federal and state-funded projects with heavy compliance requirements, who want a full construction ERP (payroll, compliance, field tracking, job costing and accounting) instead of several stitched-together tools.


### Key features


-


[Union logic](https://www.buildtrayd.com/solution/compliance/union-payroll) built into the payroll engine: CBA wage rates, fringe fund calculations and multi-local compliance


-


[Certified payroll and prevailing wage](https://www.buildtrayd.com/solution/compliance/certified-payroll) checks that run before payroll, catching classification and wage errors before they become violations


-


Field hours flow into payroll with classification, project and cost code already attached


-


Mobile onboarding in minutes, in English and Spanish


### Pros


-


One system from field time to payroll to job costing to accounting


-


Compliance enforced up front, not fixed after the fact


-


Bilingual, construction-focused support


### Cons


-


Built specifically for specialty and trade contractors, so it's less of a fit for businesses outside construction


-


The accounting module is newer than long-standing construction ERPs


## 2. Miter


Miter is a cloud-based construction platform combining payroll, HR, expenses and field operations. It was founded in 2021 and integrates with ERPs including Sage 100, Sage 300 CRE, Sage Intacct, Acumatica, Procore and QuickBooks.


**Best for:** Contractors who want construction-specific payroll that integrates tightly with an existing ERP, especially Sage or Acumatica.


### Key features


-


Fully burdened job costing that syncs to supported ERPs


-


Broad HCM suite: recruiting, learning, performance and benefits


-


Expense management (receipts, per diems, cards) tied to payroll and job costing


-


Union pay rates and prevailing wage support


### Pros


-


Strong ERP integrations


-


Wide HR feature set beyond payroll


### Cons


-


Accounting stays in a separate ERP, so you're running and paying for two systems that don't always work smoothly together


-


The broad HCM suite can be more than smaller crews need


## 3. Foundation Software


Foundation is a construction accounting and ERP platform that has served contractors since 1985, covering job costing, payroll, accounting, project management and financial reporting. More than 25,000 construction professionals use it, according to the company.


**Best for:** Mid-sized contractors who prioritize deep construction accounting and WIP reporting and don't mind a learning curve.


### Key features


-


Certified payroll, prevailing wage, union fringes and multi-state payroll


-


Granular job costing with CSI cost codes and detailed WIP reporting


-


Integration with Payroll4Construction for outsourced payroll


### Pros


-


Decades of construction accounting depth


-


Strong financial controls and WIP reporting


### Cons


-


Reviews often describe the interface as dated


-


Limited mobile functionality for field-heavy teams


-


Pricing reported from around $500/month for core modules, plus implementation costs reported at $3,000–$8,000


## 4. Payroll4Construction


Payroll4Construction is an outsourced construction payroll service from Foundation Software. Instead of running payroll in-house, contractors send hours and the service processes payroll.


**Best for:** Contractors who want to hand off construction payroll processing rather than run it themselves.


### Key features


-


Outsourced payroll processing for construction


-


Integrates with Foundation's accounting software


### Pros


-


Takes payroll processing off your team's plate


-


Built for construction rather than general business


### Cons


-


Less day-to-day control than running payroll in your own system


-


Field time tracking and job costing depend on other tools


## 5. Sage (100 Contractor / 300 CRE / Intacct)


Sage offers several construction products. Sage 100 Contractor covers payroll, job costing and accounting for small-to-mid-sized contractors. Sage 300 CRE serves larger firms with multi-company payroll and project management. Sage Intacct is cloud financial management with construction modules.


**Best for:** Larger contractors or multi-entity organizations already invested in Sage who need deep financial reporting.


### Key features


-


Established ERP with deep accounting and reporting


-


Multi-company and multi-entity support


-


Sage 300 CRE handles union fringes and certified payroll


### Pros


-


Mature, widely used accounting ecosystem


-


Large integration ecosystem


### Cons


-


Sage 100 and 300 are on-premise, with their own deployment and maintenance


-


Three products on different architectures can be confusing to choose between


-


Field time capture often needs extra configuration or third-party tools


## 6. ADP


ADP is one of the largest payroll providers in the world. ADP Run and ADP Workforce Now aren't construction-specific, but many contractors use them for payroll, multi-state tax and HR.


**Best for:** Contractors who need a large, proven payroll processor and will add construction-specific tools on top. A better fit for non-union or lightly regulated work.


### Key features


-


Multi-state tax filing across all 50 states


-


Broad HR and benefits services


-


Certified payroll through third-party integrations such as Points North


### Pros


-


Scale and a proven tax compliance infrastructure


-


Wide range of HR services


### Cons


-


Union fringes, prevailing wage and project-level payroll aren't native


-


Construction needs usually mean add-on tools, which add cost and complexity


## 7. Gusto


Gusto is a popular payroll and HR platform for small businesses. It isn't built for construction, but some very small contractors use it for straightforward payroll.


**Best for:** Very small, non-union contractors on private projects with simple payroll.


### Key features


-


Full-service payroll with automated tax filing


-


Employee and contractor payments


-


Basic HR and onboarding


### Pros


-


Easy to set up and use


-


Low cost for small teams


### Cons


-


Not designed for construction: no native union fringe, prevailing wage or certified payroll handling


-


Limited job costing for construction projects


## 8. QuickBooks Payroll


QuickBooks Payroll works with QuickBooks Online accounting, which makes it a common choice for small contractors who already do their books in QuickBooks.


**Best for:** Small non-union contractors on private projects who already use QuickBooks.


### Key features


-


Tight integration with QuickBooks Online accounting


-


Basic payroll, tax filing and time tracking


### Pros


-


Low cost of entry


-


Familiar if you already use QuickBooks


### Cons


-


Not designed for construction: union fringes, prevailing wage and certified payroll are unavailable or need manual workarounds


-


Limited job costing detail compared with construction platforms


## How to choose the right construction payroll software


-


**Start with compliance.** If you run prevailing wage jobs, file certified payroll weekly or manage union fringes across locals, those features need to be built in, not add-ons.


-


**Check the data flow.** If field time reaches payroll through paper timesheets or exports and imports, you're building in errors. The strongest platforms send hours into payroll with project, classification and cost code already attached.


-


**Compare total cost, not just the subscription.** A $50/month tool that needs $500/month of manual work costs more than a $300/month platform that removes it.


-


**Ask for references from contractors like you.** What works for a 200-person general contractor may not suit a 30-person union electrical sub.


## The bottom line


Every platform here can cut a paycheck. The difference is everything around it: catching a wage classification error before it becomes a violation, getting field hours into payroll already coded, and producing job cost reports that reflect fully burdened labor.

## **Frequently Asked Questions**


### What is the best payroll software for a construction company?


The best choice depends on your compliance requirements and crew size. For union and prevailing wage trade contractors, construction-specific platforms such as Trayd, Miter and Foundation Software handle CBA rates, certified payroll and job costing natively. Larger firms already using Sage often choose Sage 300 CRE, while small non-union contractors on private projects may only need a general tool such as Gusto or QuickBooks Payroll.


### Can generic payroll software handle construction payroll?


Generic platforms like ADP and QuickBooks can process paychecks, but they lack native support for union fringe calculations, prevailing wage management, project-level payroll, and certified payroll reporting. Most construction contractors need specialized software or add-on integrations.


### What features should construction payroll software include?


Project-level wage configuration, multi-state tax compliance, prevailing wage rate management, certified payroll (WH-347) generation, union CBA support, field-to-payroll data flow, and real-time job costing tied to fully burdened labor costs.


### How does construction payroll software connect to job costing?


When payroll and job costing share the same system or are tightly integrated, fully burdened labor costs (wages, taxes, workers' comp, benefits, union fringes) are automatically allocated to the correct project and cost code as payroll runs.


### Do construction payroll platforms handle certified payroll reporting?


Construction-specific platforms typically generate WH-347 certified payroll reports directly from payroll data. Generic platforms usually require manual report preparation or third-party integrations.


### Is construction payroll software worth the cost for small contractors?


For contractors on prevailing wage or union projects, the compliance risk of manual processes usually outweighs the software cost. For small, non-union contractors on private work, a simpler platform with basic payroll may be sufficient.
